referenceEncoder.name: mixed
referenceEncoder.note:
READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING A BYTE. This corpus has two provenances, given per vector in its `source` field.

(1) source = "cbV2G@03350be048b3 (iso_20/AC)": bytes from EVerest's libcbv2g at the pinned commit, taken verbatim from Iso15118_20.AC.vectors.json. These are messages that use no DER member, and the DER grammar was MEASURED to encode them identically to the plain AC grammar — so cbV2G is a valid oracle for them here. 6 of 10 plain-AC vectors are in this class.

(2) source = "Vanaheimr.V2G.Exi (C#)": this project's own output, NOT verified against anything. cbexigen does not generate the ISO 15118-20 Amendment 1 DER schemas, so no reference encoder exists. These vectors pin the encoding against drift and give the Kotlin port a byte target; they are not evidence of wire conformance. Two kinds land here: messages whose plain-AC members shift event code under the DER grammar, and messages that actually carry a DER member.

Header SessionID is 8x0x00, TimeStamp=1700000000, no Signature — as in the AC corpus. The fixtures are Iso15118_20AcDerSaeFixtures.
